data.name: Score frozen NY Numbers prospective test

derived_state.prompt:
Score Damian's pre-registered NY Lottery Numbers prospective test, frozen on 2026-10-15. Do not change any rule below; the point is a single, untouched analysis.

1. Download the official dataset: https://data.ny.gov/api/views/hsys-3def/rows.csv?accessType=DOWNLOAD (columns "Draw Date", "Midday Daily #", "Evening Daily #"; read as strings to keep leading zeros).
2. Frozen predictions (most frequent digit per position, window 2021-10-15..2026-10-14): midday = (5, 0, 8), evening = (5, 4, 2) for positions 1, 2, 3.
3. Take draws dated on or after 2026-10-16 in chronological order, midday before evening on each date, skipping blanks. Use exactly the first 307 draws (921 digit trials). If fewer than 307 exist, report NOT READY with the count and stop.
4. Hits = number of positions where the drawn digit equals the frozen digit for that draw time. H0: hit probability 0.10. Reject only if hits > 107 (one-sided exact binomial, alpha 0.05, 80% power at 12.6%). Report hits, hit rate, exact one-sided p, first/last dates, and the verdict.
5. Verdict meaning: fail to reject -> the recent-window bias hypothesis is not supported; recommend closing the study. Reject -> a lead only, not an edge: straight-play break-even needs about 12.6% per position (official $500 prize per $1, 1-in-1,000 odds) and front-pair needs about 14.1% (official $50 per $1, 1 in 100); a reject needs replication on new draws before any money is spent. Do not recommend buying tickets either way.
6. No interim looks, no extra tests, no re-specification. Send the result to the user as a short message.
